name: Edge-Optimized Task-Driven Detection
blurb: Hardware/software co-designed zero-shot detection SoC on a Digilent Genesys 2 (Kintex-7) with a C-DAC VEGA RV32 RISC-V host. INT8 convolution accelerator in SystemVerilog, verified bit-exact on real silicon.
detail:
Built an INT8 convolution accelerator in SystemVerilog — a 16x32 MAC tile packing 512 MACs into 256 DSP48E1 slices via 2-MAC packing, a vector unit for bias, requantisation and activation, and an elaboration-time SiLU ROM. Exposed as an AXI4 peripheral with an AXI4-Lite control slave, AXI4 burst masters to DDR3 and a descriptor-chained GEMM controller, so the VEGA host issues one kick per inference.

Added semantic pre-filtering: Model2Vec runs on VEGA in parallel with convolution, cosine-matching prompt embeddings against 80 COCO class embeddings to rank classes and score detections as conf/(rank+1), with an early-exit policy halting on the first valid detection. MiniLM (22.7M params) hit 93.1% top-1 and 100% top-3 intent resolution at 10.3 ms against a 195 ms budget, beating MobileCLIP2-B at 72.4% and 55.0 ms.

Explored a Sea of PEs 8x8 array, a Winograd fast-convolution prototype, and a multi-cluster systolic TPU variant — a 2x2 mesh of 16x16 arrays hitting 409 GOPS at 200 MHz with a 64-lane vector unit, 2D strided DMA and an XY-routed NoC.

Verified on real hardware: an 8x8 port (64 DSP48E1 PEs, 71% utilisation) under a hard 90-DSP Basys 3 budget was synthesised, placed, routed and run on-board at 100 MHz with WNS +0.287 ns, bit-exact against a NumPy golden model across 8/8 randomised trials plus edge cases. Authored the BRAM/DSP/im2col verification regression in Vivado xsim, QuestaSim and cocotb.
